designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch how a topic maps to subscribers and what each subscription stores as its inbox. Name the structure for the inbox and how unsubscribe finds itself.

parts.title: Topics and subscriptions

hints.text: What does each subscriber need so read() can return the next message without scanning other topics?
A dict of topic -> list of subscriptions, each with its own queue, is enough.
On publish, deepcopy the message into each live subscription's deque. Unsubscribe removes the sub from the topic list and flips a dead flag so read raises.

probes: Why copy the message on publish?
What happens if you publish with zero subscribers?

parts.title: Bounded queues

hints.text: When capacity is set, what do you check before enqueueing?
publish's return value is a count of successful enqueues, not of subscribers seen.
If len(queue) >= capacity, skip that sub (count 0 for it). Unbounded capacity=None never skips.

probes: Does a full subscriber block others on the same topic?

parts.title: Backpressure policy

hints.text: The decision 'what to do when full' wants to be swappable without rewriting publish.
Give each policy an offer(queue, capacity, message) -> bool (or raise).
DropOldest pops left then appends; DropNewest returns False; BlockStub raises BackpressureError.

probes: Why is BlockStub a stub and not real blocking?

criteria: policy is a seam, not if/elif sprawl
